words.asked:
**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** John: "we've not been applying quite the right force to bend the curve… now want to run both real work, and some real tidies." The Drift & Coherence and Seams & Tangles reviews of 13 Nov found this area carrying rules written in two places that disagree. Batch 1 added several of them:

* Harbour can mark a task Done on a person's check before its blind read, while another check refuses that same task, and a read is then sent to a ticket that's already Done (Drift run 7, `close-out-gate-precedence-split`). John's ruling: "if I choose to do something, Harbour is a passenger. This reflects that for many real projects, they're unlikely to be exclusively changed via Harbour."
* Two pieces of code decide which PRs belong to a task, and they disagree about agent notes, so a blind read can be offered over a PR no review covered (Seams run 12, §3.0a).
* The task timeline decides which model a dispatch used by its own rule, separate from the one the cost figures use (Drift, row 150).
* The check that makes a stage wait while another is live is a runs rule, but it lives with the prompts (Seams, P-LW1).

The area's note holds 20 Waiting entries, and `lib/dispatch-store.js` is 4,530 lines. Seams also tried moving files between areas three ways, and none made the tangle smaller.

**What we want.**

* Each rule in the area has one home, and the copies are gone.
* When a person acts, Harbour follows, and that rule is written once.
* The area's Waiting entries are settled, or each says why it can't be yet.
* Each piece finishes one move and names what it retired. John: "I'd be happy to run a small variety, erring larger, to see", so piece sizes vary, leaning larger.
* The LLM & prompts side of the seam is A14's.

**Done when**

* the cases above are settled, or John has ruled they can wait;
* the area's Waiting entries are settled or say why not;
* the area reads better in a blind read after this work than before it, by more than an untouched area read at the same times.

**Every change names what it retires. Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

fields.says: Survey @ cfd152fa4: `wakeHook.releaseNote` cannot reach most releases. The hook is built per request (`leftoverStep.forRequest`, `routes/dispatch.js:1636`, `routes/proxy-runner.js:213`) and only passed into `addFeedback`; most releases come through `_archiveItem` -> `_releaseIfHeld` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:1890`, `:1949`) from `removeItem`, `cleanup()` expiry and the stopped-run cleanup, none of which has a request or hook. Only the `_applyWakeHook` re-release (`:3429`) holds one. So put the wording on `leftoverStep` and late-bind it into the store, as `setWakeCredentialProvisionerFactory` already is (`server.js:1146`), and decide what an unbound store says (`lin-4373-leftover-step.test.js` asserts "did not run" five times). This is the second hook surface Waiting 5 (one `wakeHook`) warns about; shape it with that in mind. Do this first: it is the only part that changes the store shape, and it decides what the rewritten lin-4377 witness counts (no `formatHeldWakeNote` import in the store).

`findWakeEvent` has no skip rule to derive: it returns the last matching marker of any kind (`lib/dispatch-terminal.js:631`), and `lib/session-telemetry.js:82` calls it "Deliberately NOT shared". Deriving a filter would change the mint path (`lib/dispatch-store.js:3696`) and every reader of stored rows (task-page-loader, run-view, digest-feedback, run-loop-state), against the binding "never recompute pre-cutover history". Recommend: give the table a wake-role column ("every kind may carry a wake") and pin that current behaviour matches it, rather than adding a filter; the PR says this is how the done-when clause on `findWakeEvent` is met.

Prompt seam (LLM & prompts side is LIN-4448s): `lib/prompts/runner-kickoff.js` renders `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS` into the runner prompt in its current order, checked by `runner-kickoff.test.js:191`; a derived list must keep that exact order. The table also needs rows for kinds deliberately off the allowlist (`decision-answer`, `decision-withdrawal-reversed`; see `DECISION_LIFECYCLE_STAMP_KINDS`, `lib/session-telemetry.js:60`); without them a roles column quietly widens what the runner may post.

index.says: Every exit from the queue except a take archives through `_archiveItem` (`lib/dispatch-store.js`); a new exit must archive through it too.

The wake path is `_planWake` (decide) then `_deliverWake` (deliver) in `lib/dispatch-store.js`, shared by `addFeedback` and the held-wake release (LIN-4373). Its guards (LIN-1059, 1165, 1357, 2297, 4080, 4166) run in an order that matters: change the pair whole, keep the wake suites passing, and update the two census pins (`lin-3134-declared-mint-census`, `lin-4080-addItem-census`) if the write moves.

The store knows no leftovers (LIN-4383). It holds a parent wake by `heldWakeFor` (LIN-4373), released by the holder's terminal or `_archiveItem` under the build's guard key, so it wakes once. Leftover wording lives in `lib/dispatch-leftover-hook.js`; a new held-wake feature brings a hook (`lin-4377-store-knows-no-leftover` counts the word).

Plan piece 5 puts one `FEEDBACK_KINDS` table in `lib/dispatch-feedback-validation.js`. That file imports `dispatch-validation.js`, which reaches `session-telemetry.js` (via prompt-templates -> ... -> wall-clock-summary) and `dispatch-terminal.js` (via dispatch-fields -> dispatch-wake). If those import the table and build Sets from it at load, load order decides whether they hit a TDZ error. May the table live in a new import-free leaf module instead (e.g. `lib/dispatch-feedback-kinds.js`), imported by validation and the store, with the store still re-exporting `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS`?

Place survey @ cfd152fa4, for question-67: the cycle is nearer than the load-order chain it names. `lib/dispatch-feedback-validation.js:13` already imports its kind list (`FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS`) from `lib/dispatch-store.js`, so the dependency points the wrong way; if the store then imports a table from validation, the two import each other. Recommend the leaf: `lib/dispatch-feedback-kinds.js`, importing nothing, read by validation, the store and `lib/session-telemetry.js`, with the store keeping its `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS` re-export so callers do not move.
